facility_roles.quote: The first stage of the Cryogenic Dark Matter Search (CDMS I) operates at the Stanford Underground Facility, a tunnel 10.6 m beneath the Stanford University campus.

End: the last CDMS I data, the Ge BLIP run 'Between November, 1998, and September, 1999'.

notes: external.inspire_experiment is null: INSPIRE was not consulted (its rate budget belongs to the supervised importer).
Collaboration: the CDMS Collaboration, recorded as collaboration:cdms-ii ('CDMS Collaboration'); the papers on CDMS I are signed '(CDMS Collaboration)'.

Site: Stanford Underground Facility, a tunnel in the Hansen Experimental Physics Laboratory on the Stanford campus (not SLAC); see facility:stanford-underground-facility. The 17 m.w.e. depth made muon-induced neutrons the limiting background, the reason the apparatus moved to Soudan.
The first tower of CDMS II ZIP detectors also ran at SUF (Dec 2001 - June 2002; arXiv:1010.4290); that run is recorded as a result of experiment:cdms-ii, not here.

physics_goals.quote: The Cryogenic Dark Matter Search (CDMS) employs Ge and Si detectors to search for WIMPs via their elastic-scattering interactions with nuclei while discriminating against interactions of background particles.
physics_goals.value: Search for WIMPs through elastic scattering in Ge and Si detectors that discriminate nuclear from electron recoils

summary.plain: The first stage of the Cryogenic Dark Matter Search: germanium and silicon crystals cooled to 20 thousandths of a degree above absolute zero, in a shallow tunnel under Stanford University. Its 2000 result excluded, at more than 84% confidence, the whole dark matter signal region reported by the DAMA experiment.
summary.technical: Four 165 g Ge BLIP (NTD phonon) detectors and a 100 g Si ZIP detector measuring ionization and phonons, in a 20 mK cold volume behind 15 cm Pb, 25 cm polyethylene and a scintillator muon veto at ~17 m.w.e. (Stanford Underground Facility). 1998 Si run (33 live days) and 1998-99 Ge run (96 live days, 3 of 4 detectors; 10.6 kg d after cuts, 15.8 kg d in the later relaxed-fiducial analysis). Limits exclude unexplored space for 10-70 GeV/c^2; 23 candidates consistent with neutron background.
